literal: family (short for you have come to family)
usage: This is the most common secular way to say hello or welcome in Cairo. It is used in both casual and professional settings, regardless of religion or age. People usually follow it immediately with a question about the person's health or state.

variants.label: Islamic/Traditional
variants.note: The default greeting for many Egyptians, especially in shops or on the street.

variants.label: To a man (How are you)
variants.note: Often used as a standalone hello when greeting a male friend or acquaintance.

variants.label: To a woman (How are you)
variants.note: The female equivalent of ezzayak, used when greeting a woman.

variants.label: More welcoming
variants.note: Used when receiving guests at your home or office to show extra warmth.

responses.english: and peace be upon you (response to salam 3aleikom)

examples.english: Hello everyone, how are you doing?
